label: lr-ae3cb
summary: The network combines four effects. A saddle in systolic pressure and heart rate: high pressure with a slow heart rate raises the predicted risk (an arm read as sbp / heart_rate, concept score 0.96), a fast heart rate without high pressure raises it through a shock gate (detector concept heart_rate > 76 and sbp < 145, score 0.97), and a brake that opens with a fast rate or high pressure cancels the direct terms, so a fast heart rate with high pressure is low risk (mean predicted risk 1.2% for the 38 training patients matching heart_rate > 90 and sbp > 145). A U in serum sodium with a flat bottom, steeper on the low side, where very low sodium also opens the shock gate (mean predicted risk 58.8% for sodium < 134, 28.0% for sodium >= 134 and sodium <= 139 and 53.1% for sodium > 139). Straight-line rises with age and creatinine through direct terms, and smaller additions for smoking, diabetes and male sex; body-mass index barely matters and the noise input is unconnected. The annotated model reproduces the network (function preservation error 1.8e-15) with full structural and compositional coverage.

leaves.name: direct_terms
leaves.why: A linear sum of five risk factors (age, sbp, heart rate, creatinine, smoking), each raising risk; the concept is its own three largest terms, so it is a reading of the formula's main terms.

leaves.name: rate_pressure_brake
leaves.why: Opens with a fast heart rate or high pressure and subtracts from the score, making tachycardia protective when pressure is high; the sweep at two pressures confirms it.

leaves.name: high_sbp_low_hr_arm
leaves.why: Rises with high pressure relative to heart rate (low shock index), opening at a higher pressure the faster the heart rate; the sbp sweep at three heart rates confirms it.

leaves.name: high_hr_low_sbp_detector
leaves.why: Tachycardia detector switched off by hypertension (the raised-shock-index pattern; heart_rate / sbp is also graded meaningful), with a small old-age push; feeds the shock gate.

leaves.name: high_sodium_arm
leaves.why: Hinge that opens just above the normal sodium range (hypernatraemia arm of the U), later and smaller in the very old.

leaves.name: male_unit
leaves.why: Copy of male sex feeding the shock gate; raises risk when the gate is open.

leaves.name: smoker_unit
leaves.why: Copy of smoking with a small negative push on the shock gate; a minor part, smoking acts mainly through its direct term.

overall_function: The network adds a saddle-shaped effect of systolic pressure and heart rate (risk high for high pressure with a slow heart rate and for a fast heart rate without high pressure, low for a fast heart rate with high pressure), built from a high-pressure arm, a tachycardia detector feeding a hinge gate, and a brake that cancels the direct pressure and heart-rate terms when either is high. Serum sodium has a U-shaped effect with a flat bottom in the normal range, steeper on the low side, where very low sodium also opens the gate; high pressure with a slow heart rate makes the low-sodium hinge open at milder hyponatraemia. Age and creatinine raise risk monotonically through straight-line direct terms; smoking (mainly direct), diabetes (inside the gate, so mostly when it is open) and male sex (through the gate) add smaller increases. Body-mass index has a negligible effect and the noise input is unconnected.
clinical_terms: The model raises the predicted risk for a raised shock index (tachycardia with low or normal blood pressure) and for hypertension with a relatively slow heart rate, and lowers it for tachycardia with hypertension. It raises risk for both hyponatraemia (steeply, and more so with hypertension and bradycardia) and hypernatraemia, with the lowest risk in the normal sodium range. Older age and higher creatinine (worse renal function) raise risk throughout their ranges; smoking, diabetes and male sex add to it, diabetes and male sex mainly in the shock pattern.
stuck: Hierarchy planning: the low-sodium hinge feeds both the output and (through a relay) the shock gate, and the high-pressure arm feeds the low-sodium hinge, so the sodium composition had to be nested inside the shock-gate composition and the low-sodium hinge, relay and gate are composition-owned units rather than leaves (described and self-probed, not concept-probed). Nothing else blocked.
